title: Alibi and Inheritance
premise: Casper Nakamura, the concierge of the Grand Meridian Hotel, has spent two decades cataloguing the town of Bellhaven's secrets in a private ledger disguised as a guest register. When a nervous stranger pays a month's fee in advance to hire Casper to prove that hotel owner Edmund Voss will not be murdered, Casper's meticulous records become both weapon and target. As Voss turns up dead anyway and Casper's own alibi places them at the scene, they must decode the hidden second ledger — one that names every powerful family in town and the debts binding them — before the trial condemns an innocent maid. The killer is the victim's heir, who needed the ledger destroyed before it exposed twenty years of laundered money; Casper survives by trading the ledger's silence for justice, finally choosing found family over the town's corrupt old guard.
about_author: Wren Crane is the pen name of a former night-desk clerk who swears half the plots arrived via complaint forms. They write mysteries from a small apartment above a laundromat, alphabetizing their fears.

chapters.title: The Advance Payment
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. A rain-soaked stranger named Ilsa pays a month in advance to hire Casper to prevent a murder that hasn't happened yet — Edmund Voss's. Casper, who notices everything but intervenes in nothing, accepts out of curiosity rather than belief. Emotional beat: uneasy fascination; the first crack in twenty years of careful neutrality.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Small Secrets
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Flashback-woven chapter establishing Casper's ledger: affairs, bribes, quiet disappearances, all filed under guest initials. We meet the hotel staff Casper considers family — maid Rosa, bartender Dev, night auditor June. Emotional beat: warmth and loneliness intertwined; the ledger as both shield and cage.

chapters.title: Mr. Voss Checks In
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Edmund Voss arrives unexpectedly with his estranged son Adrian and lawyer Marguerite Hale. Tension crackles between father and son over the inheritance. Casper observes a threatening note slipped under Voss's door. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into purpose; Casper begins watching in earnest.

chapters.title: What the Night Auditor Saw
chapters.summary: POV: June. June reveals someone accessed the hotel's back office at 3 a.m. using a master key only senior staff possess. Casper realizes the threat comes from inside. Emotional beat: betrayal's cold draft; the 'family' metaphor begins to fracture.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Impossible Request
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Pressed, Ilsa admits she's Voss's illegitimate daughter, warned anonymously that he'd be killed during his stay. Casper cross-references the warning's phrasing against their ledger and finds a match: language used years ago by the town's founding families. Emotional beat: resolve hardening; the case becomes personal.

chapters.title: The Founders' Dinner
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. A gala in the ballroom gathers Bellhaven's elite — Judge Okafor, Councilman Reyes, matriarch Vivian Ashcombe. Casper works the room, noting glances, handshakes, debts acknowledged with nods. Emotional beat: claustrophobic elegance; power revealed as a web, not a ladder.

chapters.title: A Body in Room 412
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Voss is found dead, poisoned, and every scrap of evidence points to Rosa, whose fingerprints are on the decanter. Worse: the lobby camera shows Casper entering the wing minutes before. Emotional beat: vertigo — the observer becomes the observed.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Suspects
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Under police pressure from Detective Brandt, Casper secretly builds a parallel file: Adrian, Marguerite, Ilsa, Vivian, even Dev. Each has motive; each has a hole. Emotional beat: methodical grief; work as anesthesia for fear.

chapters.title: Rosa's Silence
chapters.summary: POV: Rosa. In holding, Rosa refuses to explain why her prints were on the decanter, protecting someone. Casper visits and recognizes the tell of loyalty, not guilt. Emotional beat: fierce tenderness; Casper vows the trial will never happen on false testimony.

chapters.title: The Ledger Hidden in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Casper discovers their own guest register contains a second text — marginalia in Voss's handwriting from decades past, when he was a junior clerk here too. The old man knew about Casper's habit all along. Emotional beat: eerie kinship across generations of watchers.

chapters.title: Decoding Voss
chapters.summary: POV: Casper and Ilsa. Working nights, they crack Voss's cipher: room numbers map to dates, guest initials to payments. The ledger records twenty years of money laundering funneling through the hotel to the founding families. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into danger — knowledge this big gets people killed.

chapters.title: Someone Searches My Desk
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Casper returns to find their quarters ransacked; the original register is missing pages. Only three people knew where it was kept. Trust within the hotel family collapses further. Emotional beat: paranoia blooming in a place that once felt like home.

chapters.title: Dev's Debt
chapters.summary: POV: Dev. Dev confesses he owed gambling money to men connected to Ashcombe and was forced to plant the decanter for Rosa to handle. He didn't know it would be used for murder. Emotional beat: shame and relief; confession as the price of staying family.

chapters.title: Marguerite Hale's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. The lawyer offers Casper immunity in exchange for the decoded ledger — revealing she's been Voss's silent partner for years and now needs the evidence buried before trial testimony exposes her. Emotional beat: temptation; the corrupt offer wears a reasonable face.

chapters.title: Adrian's Alibi Problem
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Adrian claims he was driving all night, but toll records place his car in town. Confronted, he breaks: he came to confront his father about disinheritance, argued, left — and saw someone else heading up to 412 wearing a staff uniform. Emotional beat: pity replacing suspicion; hatred softening into shared loss.

chapters.title: The Uniform in the Laundry
chapters.summary: POV: June. June finds a burned staff jacket in the incinerator ash with a distinctive monogram thread. It belongs to a uniform issued only to management — pointing back toward the hotel's board, and toward whoever ordered the master key used. Emotional beat: quiet triumph of small diligence over big money.

chapters.title: Ashcombe's Tea
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Casper accepts tea with Vivian Ashcombe, who speaks in velvet threats: the founding families built Bellhaven, and Bellhaven protects its builders. She offers Casper a place among them. Emotional beat: the seduction of power; love against duty made literal.

chapters.title: Trial Week
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Rosa's trial opens; prosecution's case is airtight unless the real ledger surfaces. Casper must choose: hand the decoded evidence to Brandt and expose everyone including friends, or stay silent and let Rosa hang. Emotional beat: the weight of the witness stand pressing on a professional bystander.

chapters.title: The Master Key
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Reconstructing key logs, Casper proves only one person could access 412 unseen: the person who commissioned the hotel renovation — Marguerite Hale, who poisoned Voss to erase his planned confession and pinned it on Rosa. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the mystery resolves not with a chase but with arithmetic.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Ballroom
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Casper lures Hale to the empty ballroom with a fake ledger page, recording her confession while Ashcombe's people close in to seize the evidence for themselves. Detective Brandt, tipped by Ilsa, arrests Hale — and turns on Ashcombe with the recording. Emotional beat: climax as trap within trap; courage finally outrunning caution.

chapters.title: What the Town Owes
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Fallout: Ashcombe indicted, the founding families scrambling, Rosa freed. Casper must decide the ledger's fate — exposure would burn innocent descendants along with the guilty. They redact the personal, release the criminal, keeping faith with both truth and mercy. Emotional beat: bittersweet catharsis; justice without cruelty.

chapters.title: Checkout Is at Noon
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Months later, the Grand Meridian reopens under joint ownership by its staff — Casper, June, Dev, Rosa, with Ilsa staying on. A new guest arrives with a secret in their luggage, and Casper, smiling, opens a fresh, clean register. Emotional beat: home rebuilt on chosen bonds; the watcher finally watched over, and watching gladly.
